To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phase of the m =1 mode in the outer regions of a gas disk provides a novel and robust probe of the distribution of dark matter in galaxies.

the phase of a spiral perturbation induced in an outer gas disk of a galaxy by a tidal interaction is a sensitive tracer of the scale radius of its dark matter halo, and that this phase is observable with current instrumentation.
the scale radius of dark halos can be inferred from the phase of m = 1 spiral disturbances in the outskirts of galaxies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of matter in the universe and the evolution of structure in it.

the following: (1) the distribution of dark matter in the Milky Way, (2) dark matter in the Whirlpool Galaxy (M51), (3) the formation and evolution of spiral galaxies, (4) the formation and structure of the Milky Way, and (5) the formation of the solar system.
the following: (1) the distribution of dark matter in galaxies; (2) the distribution of gas in galaxies; and (3) the relationship between the two.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scale radius of M51 is 17 +/- 3 kpc.
the scale radius of dark halos is consistent with cosmological simulations, and that the Whirlpool Galaxy is not a special case.
our method is capable of inferring the scale radius of dark halos, but that the current state of the art is insufficient to make this statement quantitatively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scale radius of dark halos is ~20 kpc for M 51, and ~30 kpc for the Milky Way, and that the method we have developed can be applied to a wide range of galaxies.

our analysis of the M51 system suggests that the dark matter halo is not truncated at the optical edge of the galaxy, as has been previously suggested by some authors, but is instead extended to at least 17 kpc, which is consistent both with the expectations from dissipation-less cosmological simulations as well as the predictions from the lensing analysis.
the dark halo of M51 has a scale radius of 16 kpc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scale radius of dark halos can be inferred from observations, without the need for detailed simulations.
the scale radius of a dark matter halo can be determined by measuring the phase of the m = l mode in a tidal disturbance in an extended disk of gas.
the scale radius of dark halos can be measured from the phase of the m = l disturbances in the outer gas disks of galaxies.
